## Behind every vaccine: The people and expertise powering Valneva Sweden


---


-


Share This Story


-
-
-
-


In conversation with – Amra


Hojlas


, Managing Director, Valneva Sweden


In vaccine manufacturing, even something as simple as washing your hands requires precision. Every step follows carefully defined procedures, and every decision carries responsibility.


The attention to detail required by those involved reflects the complexity of the work itself. Maintaining consistency requires carefully controlled processes, specialist expertise and close monitoring at every stage.


The pressure can be considerable. Producing a vaccine takes significant time, resources and contributions from many people. When difficulties arise, teams must draw on their experience and adapt to find solutions without compromising quality.


**More than a production line**


In many ways, vaccine manufacturing is as much a craft as it is a science. Living organisms can respond differently to their environment, so specialist knowledge and judgement are essential throughout production, even when following carefully controlled procedures.


Working in this kind of environment demands a deep understanding of the process, as well as a personal sense of responsibility. Decisions made throughout production can ultimately affect the people receiving the finished vaccine, creating a connection to the work that goes beyond simply following procedures.


For me, that trust is personal. I chose to receive the vaccine manufactured at our Solna site, not only because I believe in the work of our teams, but because I wanted to stand alongside colleagues involved in its production. It was a small but meaningful expression of my confidence in the work we do.


**Working towards a shared purpose**


Producing a vaccine involves far more than the work taking place on a manufacturing line. Across our two facilities in Solna, colleagues contribute at every stage, from manufacturing the vaccine’s active ingredient and preparing its final formulation to filling, quality checks, packaging and distribution.


Each function brings different skills, but none can operate in isolation. Sharing knowledge, communicating openly and responding together to challenges are essential.


This becomes particularly important when things don’t go to plan. I’ve seen colleagues from across manufacturing, quality and leadership work side by side to find solutions – that willingness to work together makes a real difference.


Everyone at Solna has an equally important contribution to make, regardless of their role or seniority. People need to feel comfortable asking questions, raising concerns and sharing ideas, knowing they will be listened to and supported.


That trust develops through how we treat one another every day. I try to remain present and approachable, and my door is always open. I have seen how breaking down barriers between teams and leadership has encouraged people to speak more freely and take greater ownership of their work.


**The dedication behind the everyday**


After almost 30 years in pharmaceutical manufacturing, what continues to motivate me is the purpose behind the work we do and the people who do that work. Vaccines offer something particularly meaningful: the opportunity to prevent disease before it occurs, helping people live healthier lives and reducing the wider burden of infectious diseases on society.


For those working in production, each day requires sustained concentration and discipline. From entering controlled environments to overseeing complex biological processes, maintaining the required standards demands consistent care, even when unexpected challenges arise.


It is this dedication and commitment that I particularly admire, returning each day with the same focus, care and determination.


The work may happen behind the scenes, but its impact extends far beyond our facilities in Solna. Behind every vaccine are people whose knowledge, decisions and dedication help turn the possibility of prevention into reality.
